parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why trichloroethanoic acid, $\text{CCl}_3\text{COOH}$, is more acidic than ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Acyl chlorides are formed by reacting carboxylic acids with thionyl chloride, $\text{SOCl}_2$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Ethanedioyl chloride, $(\text{COCl})_2$, can be prepared by reacting ethanedioic acid, $(\text{COOH})_2$, with an excess of $\text{SOCl}_2$.

Write an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Samples of $(\text{COCl})_2$ are reacted separately with an excess of warm acidified $\text{KMnO}_4\text{(aq)}$ and with $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$.

The carbon-containing product from the reaction with $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ has the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{N}_2\text{O}_2$.

Complete the boxes in Fig. 9.1 to suggest the structure of the carbon-containing product in each reaction.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 9.1

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
A polyester can be synthesised from the reaction of $(\text{COCl})_2$ with ethane-1,2-diol, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

Draw **two** repeat units of the polymer formed. Any functional groups should be displayed.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Compound **H**, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_3$, reacts with alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ to form yellow precipitate **J** but does **not** react with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(aq)}$.

The proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of **H** in $\text{CDCl}_3$ is shown in Fig. 9.2.
